city: Tianjin means the Emperor's Ford: the Yongle emperor crossed the river here on his way to take the throne and named the place in 1404. Before that it was 直沽, the Straight Port, a fishing village where the Grand Canal meets the Haihe.

Between 1860 and 1945 nine foreign powers held concessions here: Britain, France, the United States, Germany, Japan, Russia, Italy, Austria-Hungary and Belgium. No other Chinese city had that many. Each built its own streets, so the city is a museum of other people's architecture.
Tianjin is 哏儿都, the City of Jokes: the home of 相声 crosstalk comedy and of 马三立, its greatest master. Locals heckle with love. The crowd will roast him better than Ricky can.
The food is street food: 煎饼果子 (the crepe with the cracker inside) for breakfast, 狗不理 buns (1858, the shop nobody can pronounce politely), 十八街麻花 (fried dough twists the size of a forearm).

The city of firsts: China's first modern university (北洋, 1895), its first postage stamps (the Large Dragons, printed by the Tianjin customs in 1878), its first modern police force, its first international hotel (the Astor, 1863).

The Boxer summer of 1900: the Boxers took the city, the foreign concessions were besieged, the Eight Nation army stormed it in July, and the occupation government then pulled down the old city walls. The Drum Tower he passes at km 29 stands where the wall once stood.

stories.title: The ford
stories.text: He starts outside 天津大礼堂 in the Culture Centre. The city's name is the Emperor's Ford: the Yongle emperor crossed the river here in 1404 on his way to seize the throne and named the crossing. The whole marathon is a lap of a river crossing that became a city of fifteen million.

stories.title: City of firsts
stories.text: Up 友谊路 through the government quarter. Tianjin was China's laboratory for the modern: the first university (1895), the first postage stamps (the Large Dragons, 1878, printed by the customs house), the first telegraph line, the first tram, the first modern police. Beijing ruled; Tianjin tried things.

stories.title: Into the Five Avenues
stories.text: 马场道 is Racecourse Road, named for the British racecourse that stood at its end. It leads into 五大道, the Five Avenues: two thousand garden villas built between 1900 and 1940 by the people who ran the concessions, the generals who lost and the ministers who retired. Locals call it the ten thousand nations' architecture exhibition.

stories.title: Eric Liddell's stadium
stories.text: A runner's story, 300 metres to his right: 民园体育场, the Minyuan stadium. Eric Liddell, the Chariots of Fire man, was born in Tianjin in 1902, won the 400 metres at the 1924 Paris Olympics after refusing to run his heat on a Sunday, then came back here to teach and in 1925 helped redesign this stadium on the plans of Stamford Bridge. He died in a Japanese internment camp in 1945, having given his place on a rescue boat to a pregnant woman. The track is rebuilt (2012); the man is why it exists.

stories.title: The last emperor next door
stories.text: A kilometre to the north, on 鞍山道 in the old Japanese concession, is 静园, the Garden of Serenity. 溥仪 Puyi, the last emperor, thrown out of the Forbidden City in 1924, lived in Tianjin from 1925 to 1931: first at 张园, then at 静园 from 1929. He bought cars, cameras and watches, danced at the Astor with Empress 婉容 Wanrong, and waited for a comeback. In November 1931 the Japanese smuggled him out of the city by boat to make him the puppet emperor of Manchukuo. Serenity was the wrong name.

stories.title: The Astor
stories.text: 小白楼 and the 利顺德大饭店, the Astor Hotel, 1863, China's first international hotel. Herbert Hoover stayed in 1899 as a young mining engineer before anyone had heard of him. Sun Yat-sen was a guest. Puyi danced in the ballroom. The cage elevator with the wrought-iron gate still works. Across the road, the statue of General 张自忠 Zhang Zizhong, the highest-ranking Chinese general killed fighting Japan, 1940. The 5 km station is right here.

stories.title: The river
stories.text: 台儿庄路, the Haihe on his left for the next eight kilometres. The Haihe is 72 km long and five rivers and the Grand Canal feed it. For six hundred years it carried the grain that fed Beijing; the barges came up this water and the emperors ate. Then the gunboats came up it in 1858.

stories.title: Zhigu
stories.text: 大直沽, Great Zhigu: the oldest named place on the course. Zhigu, the Straight Port, is what this town was called before it was Tianjin, a salt and fish village on the bend of the river. Water, toilets and medical at 7.5 km.

stories.title: Tianjin Bay
stories.text: 天津湾, Tianjin Bay: the glass towers and the marina. Old money on the Five Avenues, new money here. The river is the same water either way.

stories.title: The forts downstream
stories.text: 富民桥 and the 10 km station. Downstream, where this river meets the sea, stand the 大沽 Dagu forts. The British and French fought them in 1858, 1859 and 1860, lost one battle and won two, and the Treaty of Tianjin that followed opened the city as a treaty port. Every concession on this course grew from those forts falling.

stories.title: The far corner
stories.text: The 鄱阳路 turnaround, 12.5 km, the farthest point from the finish on the whole course. Water, food, toilets, medical. From here everything is, in a geographic sense, homeward.

stories.title: 春意桥
stories.text: 春意桥, the Spring Bridge, the first real ramp since the gate, and the crossing to the east bank. Nine straight kilometres of 海河东路 now, the river on his left, the city centre slowly rising ahead.

stories.title: The locomotive
stories.text: The steam locomotive monument by the river at 15 km. China's first proper railway ran here: the Kaiping line from the Tangshan coal mines reached Tianjin in 1888 and 老龙头 station, the first Tianjin station, opened the same year, where 天津站 stands today at 22.5 km. He is running the route of the first train.

stories.title: The sailors' goddess
stories.text: 金阜桥 and the 元明清天妃宫遗址博物馆, the site of a temple to 妈祖 Mazu, the sailors' goddess, from the Yuan dynasty. The saying is: first there was the Mazu temple, then there was Tianjin. The grain fleets prayed here before the Haihe. The half-marathon runners peel off at 金茂汇 in a few hundred metres.

stories.title: Halfway
stories.text: The half mat at 金汇桥. The half-marathoners go left to their medals and their 早茶; he goes straight on. The second half of a marathon starts at 30 km; this is just where the counting flips.

stories.title: Tianjin Station
stories.text: 海河广场, 天津站 across the water. The first station here opened in 1888; this one was rebuilt for the 2008 high-speed line, which does Beijing in thirty minutes. Water, food, toilets, medical at 22.5 km.

stories.title: The Century Clock and the Bridge of All Nations
stories.text: 世纪钟, the Century Clock: forty metres of brass and iron put up for the millennium, with the zodiac around the face. Beside it 解放桥, the Liberation Bridge, finished in 1927 as 万国桥, the Bridge of All Nations, because nine nations' concessions met at this river; it cost 1.9 million taels of silver and it still opens for ships. The loudest crowd of the day is here.

stories.title: The Italian concession
stories.text: 胜利路 and the 意式风情区: the Italian concession, 1902 to 1943, the only one Italy ever held in Asia, restored street by street. 梁启超 Liang Qichao, the reformer who tried to modernise the Qing in 1898 and fled, wrote his last books in his 饮冰室, the Ice-Drinker's Studio, two streets from here. The playwright 曹禺 Cao Yu grew up a few blocks away.

stories.title: 金汤桥, 15 January 1949
stories.text: 金汤桥, the oldest steel bridge on the river, 1906. At five in the morning on 15 January 1949 the two columns of the People's Liberation Army, one from the east, one from the west, met in the middle of this bridge, and Tianjin fell in 29 hours. The 25 km station is here.

stories.title: The northern turn
stories.text: 五马路 and the turnaround at 元纬路, the northernmost point. 27 km. Behind him the old city and the river junction; ahead the one climb of the day.

stories.title: The Tianjin Eye
stories.text: 永乐桥, the Yongle Bridge, named after the emperor who named the city, with 天津之眼, the Tianjin Eye, built on top of it in 2008: 120 metres, the only Ferris wheel in the world standing on a bridge. Just upstream is 三岔河口, the three-river junction where the Grand Canal meets the Haihe and where Tianjin began. The bridge is the one real hill. Water, food and medical at 27.5.

stories.title: Old Culture Street and the Mazu temple
stories.text: 北门外大街, the North Gate road, with 古文化街 just east: the Ancient Culture Street, and in it 天后宫, the Mazu temple of 1326, the oldest building in Tianjin, built for the sailors of the grain fleet. Down the street, 狗不理 buns since 1858 and 十八街麻花. He may not stop.

stories.title: The Drum Tower and the city of jokes
stories.text: 城厢中路 and 鼓楼, the Drum Tower, the centre of the walled city of 1404. The walls came down in 1900, pulled down by the foreign occupation government after the Boxer siege; the tower was rebuilt in 2001. This is the home ground of 相声, crosstalk comedy, and of 马三立, its master; Tianjin calls itself 哏儿都, the City of Jokes. The crowd here will heckle him with affection and better timing than Ricky.

stories.title: 30 km
stories.text: 南马路, the 30 km station. Marathons are decided here, not at the finish. 霍元甲 Huo Yuanjia, the martial artist of the Jet Li film Fearless, was a Tianjin man, born in 1868 a few kilometres south; he founded 精武 and died at 42. Fight the next twelve kilometres like him.

stories.title: Nankai
stories.text: 南开 district. 南开中学, Nankai Middle School, founded in 1904, where a boy called 周恩来 Zhou Enlai studied and where the future premier first spoke in public. Its founder 张伯苓 Zhang Boling asked in 1908 when China would host an Olympics; it took a hundred years.

stories.title: 长江道
stories.text: 长江道, Yangtze Road, a long straight west through residential Nankai; 32.5 km station just behind him, 35 km ahead. The least famous kilometres of the course and the ones that decide it.

stories.title: 35 km
stories.text: 红旗路, Red Flag Road, and the full 35 km station: refreshment, food, timing mat. If the wall comes, it knocks here. The old 天拖 tractor works stood on this side of the city; the science park replaced it.

stories.title: Two universities
stories.text: 大学道, University Road, with 南开大学 on one side (1919, 周恩来 among its first students, founder 张伯苓 the father of China's Olympic dream) and 天津大学 on the other, which began as 北洋大学 in 1895, the first modern university in China. Twenty thousand students who could not do what he is doing. Water, food and medical at 37.5.

stories.title: Zhou Enlai
stories.text: 复康路, and ahead by the park the 周恩来邓颖超纪念馆, the memorial to Zhou Enlai and his wife 邓颖超 Deng Yingchao. They met in Tianjin in 1919 in a student group called the Awakening Society; he became the premier for 27 years, she a leader in her own right. Their ashes were scattered, so this is the only place to visit them.

stories.title: The Water Park and the Tower
stories.text: 水上公园西路, the Water Park on his left: lakes, islands and the zoo, built in the 1950s, the biggest park in the city. Across the water, 天塔, the Tianjin TV tower, 415 metres, 1991, one of the tallest towers on earth and the only one standing in a lake. Three kilometres to go.

stories.title: The Water Drop
stories.text: 宾水西道, 41 km, medical only, and the finish comes into view: 天津奥林匹克中心, the Water Drop, 60,000 seats, built in 2007 for the Beijing Olympics' football matches and the 2013 East Asian Games. The gate was 41 km ago.

stories.title: The finish
stories.text: The last 195 metres along the stadium. The Emperor's Ford, the nine concessions, the last emperor, the Olympian born here, the bridges, the Drum Tower, and him: a first marathon finished in Tianjin.
